title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄序
皇上握符御極于茲十年夙夜孜
孜以進賢爲急申布
功令振滌濊習
德意飇馳海内喁喁嚮風唯是貴
陽西南裔壤去
神京幾萬里
===
上所以搜奇亙陋者尤切歲届壬
午復當大比士巡按監察御
史傅〔順孫〕寔綱紀之四方文
學博士應聘咸至以〔衮〕與孫
繼先主考試譚〔時進〕孫〔桴〕倫
大經同考試提調則以屬布
政司左布政使沈〔人种〕左叅
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄序
皇上握符御極，于茲十年，夙夜孜孜，以進賢爲急。申布功令，振滌濊習，德意飇馳，海内喁喁嚮風。唯是貴陽西南裔壤，去神京幾萬里，上所以搜奇亙陋者尤切。歲届壬午，復當大比士，巡按監察御史傅〔順孫〕寔綱紀之。四方文學博士應聘咸至，以〔衮〕與孫繼先主考試，譚〔時進〕、孫〔桴〕、倫大經同考試。提調則以屬布政司左布政使沈〔人种〕、左叅
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

It has now been ten years since His Majesty took hold of the imperial talisman and ascended the throne. From dawn to dusk He has been tirelessly diligent, treating the advancement of worthy men as His most urgent task. He has promulgated the examination regulations and swept away corrupt practices; as His benevolent intentions speed forth like a whirlwind, all within the seas look up eagerly toward His transforming influence. Now Guiyang is a frontier territory in the southwest, nearly ten thousand li distant from the Divine Capital, yet His Majesty's concern to search out extraordinary talent and reach into rustic obscurity [?] is especially earnest. When the year reached renwu (1582), it was once again time for the triennial examination of scholars, and Regional Investigating Censor Fu Shunsun 傅順孫 actually directed and oversaw the proceedings. Erudites of Literature from all quarters arrived in response to invitations: Gun 衮 and Sun Jixian 孫繼先 were appointed to serve as Examiners, while Tan Shijin 譚時進, Sun Fu 孫桴, and Lun Dajing 倫大經 served as Associate Examiners. The duties of Proctor were assigned to Left Administration Commissioner Shen Renzhong 沈人种 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
議詹貞吉而按察司副使鄭
秉厚僉事胡宥司監試焉餘
各錯釆有差乃進提學副使
馮時可暨湖廣參議龍宗武
所選士九百有奇三試之得
儁三十人籍氏名與文之雅
正者爲録以
===
獻衮不佞以職事當序首簡廼
論次御史意諗于多士曰衮
觀貴州之舉士也盖歎天地
與人交相感云夫風氣轉移
運行有漸山川鍾毓發洩有
期人士感奮鼓舞有待勢若
相懸而機寔相貫者也鴻荒
punctuated:
議詹貞吉，而按察司副使鄭秉厚、僉事胡宥司監試焉，餘各錯采有差。乃進提學副使馮時可暨湖廣參議龍宗武所選士九百有奇，三試之，得儁三十人，籍氏名與文之雅正者爲録以獻。

衮不佞，以職事當序首簡，廼論次御史意，諗于多士曰：衮觀貴州之舉士也，盖歎天地與人交相感云。夫風氣轉移，運行有漸；山川鍾毓，發洩有期；人士感奮，鼓舞有待。勢若相懸，而機寔相貫者也。鴻荒
translation_en:
… Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Zhan Zhenji 詹貞吉, while Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zheng Binghou 鄭秉厚 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Hu You 胡宥 of the Surveillance Commission were in charge of monitoring the examination; the remaining officials were variously assigned duties according to their rank. Thereupon, more than nine hundred scholars selected by Education-intendant Vice Commissioner Feng Shike 馮時可 and Huguang Administration Vice Commissioner Long Zongwu 龍宗武 were admitted and tested in three sessions, yielding thirty men of outstanding talent. Their names and those of their essays that were elegant and orthodox were compiled into a record for presentation to the throne.

I, [He] Gun 衮, though unworthy, am by virtue of my office obliged to write the preface at the head of the volume. I therefore set forth in order the Censor's intent and address the many scholars, saying: When I, Gun, observe the selection of scholars in Guizhou, I am moved to sigh in admiration at how Heaven, Earth, and Man mutually respond to one another. Now, the transformation of customs and cultural ethos moves forward by gradual stages; the concentration and nurturing of vital energy in mountains and rivers has its appointed time for release; and the rousing and inspiration of scholars and gentlemen awaits its proper occasion. In outward circumstance they seem far apart, yet in their underlying mechanism they are truly interconnected. In primeval times …

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
文皇之初渾渾噩噩貴與中土奚
別也自清淑之氣肇開聖賢
所生
帝王所莅遂爲文明之域茲地曰
鬼方曰夜郎若照臨不及焉
者
高皇帝混一寰宇升諸版籍而後
===
參井之野曶爽闇昧得麗於
光明斯非剖洪濛而闢
日月耶地屬荒服莫得要領而山
川圖誌又禹貢職方所不紀
箐穴蒸欝褀就且難矧云郡
縣
文皇帝樹藩設學而後隍池亭候
punctuated: 之初，渾渾噩噩，貴與中土奚別也？自清淑之氣肇開，聖賢所生、帝王所莅，遂爲文明之域。茲地曰鬼方、曰夜郎，若照臨不及焉者。高皇帝混一寰宇，升諸版籍，而後參井之野，曶爽闇昧，得麗於光明。斯非剖洪濛而闢日月耶？地屬荒服，莫得要領，而山川圖誌，又《禹貢》、《職方》所不紀；箐穴蒸欝，褀就且難，矧云郡縣？文皇帝樹藩設學，而後隍池亭候，
translation_en: …beginning [of primeval chaos], everything was simple and unformed; how then was Guizhou any different from the Central Lands? Once the pure and auspicious vital energies first opened up, the places where sages and worthies were born and where emperors and kings presided thereupon became realms of civilization. This region was called Guifang or Yelang, as though the illumination from above did not reach it. After the High Emperor [the Hongwu Emperor, Zhu Yuanzhang] unified the world and entered this land into the population and land registers, the wilderness under the constellations Shen and Jing—once dim at daybreak and shrouded in darkness—was able to attach itself to the brilliant light. Was this not cleaving primordial chaos to open up the sun and moon? The region belonged to the wild zone beyond civilization, where no governing grasp of its essentials could be had, and the maps and records of its mountains and rivers were furthermore unrecorded in the Tribute of Yu (Yugong) and the Directions of the Domain (Zhifang). With its bamboo thickets and caverns steaming andDank, even to settle there for a full year [?] was difficult, how much more so to speak of establishing commanderies and counties? After the Cultured Emperor [the Yongle Emperor, Zhu Di] established the provincial administration and founded schools, the moats, walls, post pavilions, and watchtowers…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
星聯棊布嵂崒濴洄若增而
高若濬而深壯哉一都會矣
士徙中夏世稱實塞然羅甸
八番之陋刻木擊銅吹匏頓
地左言雕結猶夫故也
肅皇帝專科廣額人文丕變我
皇上弘敷賁飭聲教四達貴之文
===
獻寖與上國埒蓋天發其祥
地呈其秀人應其期盛矣哉
自載籍以來未之覯也〔眾〕始
應聘入境也竊自念傳稱齊
魯嫺于文學其天性然也惟
玆遜土獷而習之曷易言嫺
及獲縱觀其文通經術明世
punctuated: 星聯棊布，嵂崒濴洄，若增而高，若濬而深，壯哉一都會矣！士徙中夏，世稱實塞，然羅甸、八番之陋，刻木、擊銅、吹匏、頓地、左言、雕結，猶夫故也。肅皇帝專科廣額，人文丕變；我皇上弘敷賁飭，聲教四達，貴之文獻寖與上國埒。蓋天發其祥，地呈其秀，人應其期，盛矣哉，自載籍以來未之覯也！〔眾〕始應聘入境也，竊自念傳稱「齊魯嫺于文學，其天性然也」。惟玆遜土，獷而習之，曷易言嫺？及獲縱觀其文，通經術，明世
translation_en:
…were linked like stars and arrayed like pieces on a chessboard; the precipitous peaks and swirling waters seemed built ever higher and dredged ever deeper—magnificent indeed, a true metropolis! Scholars were relocated here from the Central Plains, a policy known through the generations as filling the frontiers; yet the crude customs of Luodian and the Eight Barbarian Tribes (Bafan)—notching wood to keep records, beating bronze drums, blowing gourd pipes, stamping the ground, speaking barbarian tongues, and tattooing the body or wearing mallet-shaped topknots—remained just as they had been of old. When the Emperor Su [the Jiajing Emperor] established an independent provincial examination for Guizhou and expanded its quota, literary culture underwent a great transformation. Now Our Sovereign on High has broadly diffused civilizing grace and strict order, so that His transformative influence reaches in all four directions, and the scholarly learning and worthy talents of Guizhou have gradually come to rival those of the central provinces. Truly, Heaven has sent down its auspicious signs, Earth has brought forth its finest flowering, and human talent has risen to meet the appointed age—how flourishing indeed, something never before witnessed since written records began!

When I, Zhong, first accepted the invitation to serve and entered the borders of the province, I privately reflected on the historical tradition that says, "The people of Qi and Lu are refined in literature and learning; such is their innate nature." In a remote and humble land like this, where people must be broken of their wildness and accustomed to instruction, how could one easily speak of literary refinement? Yet when I was able to survey their examination essays at length, I found that they mastered the art of the Classics, understood the affairs of the age…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
務翩翩稱引澤於理道往往
有不盡收之恨則又肅然
北嚮歎曰我
皇上鼓舞之神一至若哉蓋風氣
所不能囿疆域所不能限者
乎史所稱啓迪鴻化緝熙康
又光照六幽翔海表而行鬼
===
區者何以加焉旣又自思曰
皇上方以久道化天下遘奇際盛
自玆伊始愈隆愈浹無俟揄
揚顧多士以言進御史暨百
執事所籍以宣
上德意圖報塞萬一者亦惟多士
之言爾矣言發于心而寔因
punctuated: 務，翩翩稱引，澤於理道，往往有不盡收之恨。則又肅然北嚮歎曰：「我皇上鼓舞之神，一至若哉！蓋風氣所不能囿、疆域所不能限者乎！史所稱啓迪鴻化、緝熙康乂，光照六幽、翔海表而行鬼區者，何以加焉！」旣又自思曰：「皇上方以久道化天下，遘奇際盛，自玆伊始，愈隆愈浹，無俟揄揚。顧多士以言進，御史暨百執事所籍以宣上德意、圖報塞萬一者，亦惟多士之言爾矣。言發于心，而寔因
translation_en: …affairs, gracefully citing precedents and steeped in the principles of governance, so that we often regretted not being able to select them all. Thereupon, I respectfully faced north and sighed: "How wondrously transformative is Our Majesty's encouragement to have reached such a degree as this! Surely this is something that local customs cannot confine and territorial boundaries cannot limit! What the histories praise as initiating great transformation, continuing luminous peace and order [reading 乂 for 又], shining light into the six obscure directions, soaring beyond the seas, and reaching into the realms of ghosts—how could that surpass this?" Then again, I reflected to myself: "His Majesty is just now transforming the realm through long-enduring principles. Encountering such extraordinary times and meeting such flourishing prosperity is only beginning from this moment; it grows ever grander and ever more pervasive, without any need for our eulogies. Yet the many scholars advance through their words, and what the Censor and all the officiating functionaries rely upon to proclaim His Majesty's virtuous intentions and to endeavor to repay even one ten-thousandth of his grace is likewise nothing other than the words of these many scholars. Words issue from the heart, yet they truly depend…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
乎時者也結繩而後六經毋
論巳春秋迄于西京雄渾冲
粹非後世所能及者則以去
古未遠耳貴俗顓蒙淳樸未
鑿斯亦去古未遠者也珠聯
綺合郎匪性嫺然而涵濡
聖化應期而興若戴勝鳴春蟋蟀
===
鳴秋不知其然而然者其不
以奇衺險僻相衒貿喑哢藻
績相剽襲也庶幾有可必者
乎夫文載道之器也志趨道
之的也學致道之準也志向
端則學術正學術正則綜述
精斌斌乎慥慥乎措之事業
punctuated: 乎時者也。結繩而後，六經毋論巳。春秋迄于西京，雄渾冲粹，非後世所能及者，則以去古未遠耳。貴俗顓蒙，淳樸未鑿，斯亦去古未遠者也。珠聯綺合，郎匪性嫺，然而涵濡聖化，應期而興，若戴勝鳴春、蟋蟀鳴秋，不知其然而然者。其不以奇衺險僻相衒貿、喑哢藻績相剽襲也，庶幾有可必者乎！夫文，載道之器也；志，趨道之的也；學，致道之準也。志向端則學術正，學術正則綜述精，斌斌乎，慥慥乎，措之事業，
translation_en: …upon the times. After the era of knotted cords, the Six Classics need not even be mentioned. From the Spring and Autumn period down to the Western Capital [Western Han], writing was vigorous, profound, harmonious, and pure, such that later ages could not match it—and this was simply because it was not yet far removed from antiquity. The customs of Guizhou are simple and unspoiled, pure and unadorned by artifice; this too is a case of not being far removed from antiquity. Though stringing pearls and weaving brocades [in ornate composition] may not[?] be something they are naturally skilled at, yet soaked and nourished by the Sacred teaching, they rise up in response to the times, just as the hoopoe calls in spring and the cricket chirps in autumn, doing so without knowing how or why. That they will not peddle and show off strange, perverse, obscure, and eccentric styles to one another, nor plagiarize from one another with incoherent chirping andflorid embellishments—may we not almost be certain of this? Now, literature is the vessel that carries the Way; resolution is the target aimed at the Way; learning is the standard for attaining the Way. When one's aspirations are upright, one's scholarship is correct; when one's scholarship is correct, one's synthesis and exposition are refined. Accomplished in both substance and style, earnest and sincere, when applied to practical endeavors, it will be…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
裕如矣是曰眞才是曰實用
皇上所籲俊登彥丕隆治理者唯
此主司所矢公殫慮冀副任
使者亦唯此多士辨之哉雖
然生瘠土者嚮義見異物者
多遷言專本業而一念慮也
貴水不涵渟土無貨殖僻在
===
遠徼綺麗鮮椄蓋服勞而能
儉者一旦去澳濼騁
天衢得毋志奪紛華而修忘窮巷
者乎澹泊是甘寧靜是勵始
終崇庳惟知精白靖共雅志
弗渝庶今日賓言自
獻者可無負以人事
punctuated: 裕如矣。是曰眞才，是曰實用。皇上所籲俊登彥，丕隆治理者，唯此；主司所矢公殫慮，冀副任使者，亦唯此。多士辨之哉！雖然，生瘠土者嚮義，見異物者多遷，言專本業而一念慮也。貴水不涵渟，土無貨殖，僻在遠徼，綺麗鮮椄，蓋服勞而能儉者。一旦去澳濼，騁天衢，得毋志奪紛華，而修忘窮巷者乎？澹泊是甘，寧靜是勵，始終崇庳，惟知精白靖共，雅志弗渝，庶今日賓言自獻者，可無負以人事
translation_en:
…with ample ease. This is called genuine talent; this is called practical utility. What the Emperor seeks in calling forth the outstanding and promoting the accomplished so as to greatly advance governance is solely this; what the chief examiners seek in swearing impartiality and exhausting their thoughts in hopes of living up to their commission is likewise solely this. May you many scholars discern this!

Even so, those born in barren lands incline toward righteousness, while those exposed to novel things often shift in their intentions—which is to say that one should concentrate on one's fundamental calling and unify one's thoughts. In Guizhou, the waters do not gather in deep pools, the land yields no commercial wealth, and lying secluded on the distant frontier, it rarely comes into contact with fine luxuries; thus its people are accustomed to toil and capable of frugality. Once they leave their secluded marshes and gallop forth onto the Imperial Highway, might their resolve not be carried away by bustling splendor, and their self-cultivation forget the humble lanes from which they came? If they find sweetness in simple living and strive for tranquility, whether from beginning to end or in high or lowly station knowing only to remain pure, upright, and quietly devoted to their duties without altering their noble aspirations, then we who today present them as honored guests with our words will perhaps not fail the principle of serving…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
君之義而協應文明宣卲靈秀蕞
爾貴筑人傑競奮寖爲海内
重矣其懋之哉是舉也前巡
撫近移鎮南贛右副都御史
王緝德澤覃敷士胥涵育今
巡撫右副都御史劉庠風猷
首勵敎益振興大理寺右寺
===
正陳明經折刑甫竣鎮守總
兵官署都督僉事胡守仁攺
秩戒行右叅政兼僉事蘇愚
右叅議秦舜翰副使華啓直
李薦佳綜理惟周署都指揮
僉事劉招桂蔡兆吉左叅將
馬呈文右叅將張奇峯飭防
punctuated: 君之義，而協應文明，宣卲靈秀，蕞爾貴筑，人傑競奮，寖爲海内重矣。其懋之哉！是舉也，前巡撫、近移鎮南贛右副都御史王緝德澤覃敷，士胥涵育；今巡撫右副都御史劉庠風猷首勵，敎益振興；大理寺右寺正陳明經折刑甫竣；鎮守總兵官、署都督僉事胡守仁攺秩戒行；右叅政兼僉事蘇愚、右叅議秦舜翰、副使華啓直、李薦佳綜理惟周；署都指揮僉事劉招桂、蔡兆吉，左叅將馬呈文，右叅將張奇峯飭防…
translation_en:
…the duty of serving the Ruler [by recommending worthy men], and in harmonious response to civilizing enlightenment, spread and exalt its numinous refinement, so that even in tiny Guizhu, outstanding talents will vie to rouse themselves, gradually coming to be esteemed throughout the realm. Strive earnestly toward this!

In this undertaking, the former Grand Coordinator, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wang Ji 王緝, recently transferred to the defense command of Nan-Gan, broadly spread his virtuous beneficence, by which the scholars were all nurtured; the current Grand Coordinator, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiang 劉庠, took the lead in encouraging moral governance, whereby education was further revitalized; Right Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Mingjing 陳明經 had just concluded his adjudication of penal cases; the Grand Defender and Regional Commander, Acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Hu Shouren 胡守仁, was preparing to depart upon reassignment to a new post; Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Su Yu 蘇愚, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Qin Shunhan 秦舜翰, and Surveillance Vice Commissioners Hua Qizhi 華啓直 and Li Jianjia 李薦佳 managed the overall administration with thoroughness; Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Liu Zhaogui 劉招桂 and Cai Zhaoji 蔡兆吉, Left Assistant Regional Commander Ma Chengwen 馬呈文, and Right Assistant Regional Commander Zhang Qifeng 張奇峯 maintained the security defenses…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
惟謹若左布政使錢藻移任
於楚左叅政史樌副使段孟
賢署都指揮僉事楊雲程馳
賀於
京皆先事與勞例得備書云
直隸徽州府儒學教授黃裦
謹序
punctuated:
惟謹。若左布政使錢藻移任於楚，左叅政史樌、副使段孟賢、署都指揮僉事楊雲程馳賀於京，皆先事與勞，例得備書云。
直隸徽州府儒學教授黃裦謹序。
translation_en:
…with utmost diligence. As for Left Administration Commissioner Qian Zao 錢藻, who was transferred to a post in Chu [Huguang], as well as Left Administration Vice Commissioner Shi Guan 史樌, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Duan Mengxian 段孟賢, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Yang Yuncheng 楊雲程, who rode post to the capital to present congratulations—all contributed their labors beforehand and by precedent ought to be recorded in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Huang Bao 黃裦, Confucian School Instructor of Huizhou Prefecture in the Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili).

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年貴州鄉試

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰莫我知也夫子貢曰何爲其莫知子
也子曰不怨天不尤人下學而上達知
我者其天乎
道不遠人人之爲道而遠人不可以爲道
君子之守脩其身而天下平
易
舍弘光大品物咸亨
===
惠我德大得志也
鼓之以雷霆潤之以風雨日月運行一寒
一暑
聚而上者謂之升
書
帝曰俞允若玆嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬
邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不
廢困窮惟帝時克
惟暨乃僚罔不同心以匡乃辟
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
子曰：「莫我知也夫！」子貢曰：「何爲其莫知子也？」子曰：「不怨天，不尤人，下學而上達。知我者，其天乎！」
道不遠人。人之爲道而遠人，不可以爲道。
君子之守，脩其身而天下平。

易
舍弘光大，品物咸亨。
惠我德，大得志也。
鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨。日月運行，一寒一暑。
聚而上者謂之升。

書
帝曰：「俞！允若玆，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。」
惟暨乃僚，罔不同心，以匡乃辟。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

The Master said, "Alas, there is no one who knows me!" Zigong said, "Why is it that no one knows you?" The Master said, "I do not complain against Heaven, nor do I blame men. I study what is below and attain to what is above. The one who knows me—is it not Heaven?"

The Way is not far from man. When men pursue a way that distances them from man, it cannot be considered the Way.

What the gentleman holds fast to is cultivating his person so that the world is brought to peace.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Containing all in its breadth [reading 含 for 舍] and shining forth in its greatness, all things in their categories attain smooth success.

"They are kind to my virtue"—this means greatly fulfilling one's aspirations.

Rousing them with thunder and lightning, moistening them with wind and rain; the sun and moon move in their courses, bringing now cold, now heat.

Gathering together and rising upward is called Ascending (Sheng).

Book of Documents (Shu)

The Sovereign said, "Yes! Truly, if it is like this, admirable words will nowhere lie hidden, no worthy men will be left overlooked in the wilds, and the myriad states will all enjoy peace. To consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and impoverished—only the former Sovereign was able to do this."

Together with your colleagues, let none fail to be of one heart in assisting your sovereign.

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
明王愼德四夷咸賔無有遠邇畢獻方物
惟服食器用
德威惟畏德明惟明乃命三后恤功于民
伯夷降典折民惟刑禹平水土主名山
川稷降播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷
于民士制百姓于刑之中以敎祗德穆
穆在上明明在下灼于四方罔不惟德
之勤故乃明于刑之中率乂于民棐彝
詩
螽斯羽詵詵兮宜爾子孫振振兮
===
旄維旟矣室家溱溱
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸塈
昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢康夙夜
基命宥密於緝熙單厥心肆其靖之
春秋
冬天王使宰周公來聘僖公三十年春宋
公使華元來聘成公四年
公會齊侯于城濮莊公二十七年
punctuated:
「明王愼德，四夷咸賔，無有遠邇，畢獻方物，惟服食器用。」
「德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后，恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以敎祗德。穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。故乃明于刑之中，率乂于民，棐彝。」
《詩》：
「螽斯羽，詵詵兮；宜爾子孫，振振兮。」
「旄維旟矣，室家溱溱。」
「百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸塈。」
「昊天有成命，二后受之。成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。於緝熙，單厥心，肆其靖之。」
《春秋》：
「冬，天王使宰周公來聘。」（僖公三十年）「春，宋公使華元來聘。」（成公四年）
「公會齊侯于城濮。」（莊公二十七年）
translation_en:
"When the enlightened king carefully attends to his virtue, the barbarian tribes on all four sides all come as guests. Far and near alike, they all present their local products—only garments, foodstuffs, and vessels for use."

"Through the majesty of his virtue they were awed; through the brightness of his virtue they were enlightened. He then commanded the Three Princes to labor with compassionate care for the people: Boyi 伯夷 handed down the statutes, restraining the people through punishments; Yu 禹 regulated the waters and the land, presiding over the naming of mountains and rivers; and Ji 稷 handed down the arts of sowing, cultivating the fine grains. When the Three Princes had accomplished their work, there was abundance among the people. The Chief Justice regulated the hundred surnames through the just mean of punishments, so as to teach reverence for virtue. Profound and reverent was the sovereign above, bright and discerning were the ministers below; shining forth to the four quarters, none failed to be diligent in virtue. Thus they were clear in the just mean of punishments, leading and governing the people, and aiding their constant nature."

Book of Odes (Shi 詩):

"The wings of the locusts, how they throng together! Well may your sons and grandsons be numerous and noble!"

"The tortoise-and-snake banners have become falcon banners; the households and families are thronging and populous."

"All the feudal lords and noble ministers show love to the Son of Heaven; never lax in their positions, through them the people find rest."

"August Heaven had a settled mandate, which the two sovereigns received. King Cheng 成王 did not dare to rest in comfort; morning and night he laid the foundations of the mandate in breadth and quietness. Oh! Continuing the bright glory, he exhausted his heart, and so brought peace to it."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋):

"In winter, the Heavenly King sent the Grand宰, the Duke of Zhou 周公, to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" (30th year of Duke Xi 僖公); "In spring, the Duke of Song 宋公 sent Hua Yuan 華元 to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" (4th year of Duke Cheng 成公).

"The Duke met the Marquis of Qi 齊侯 at Chengpu 城濮" (27th year of Duke Zhuang 莊公).

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
遂伐楚次于陘　楚屈完來盟于師盟于
召陵僖公四年公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹
伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚襄公十一年夏
楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓
子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會
于申昭公四年
宋公伐邾昭公十九年夏曹公孫會自鄸
出奔宋昭公二十年
===
禮記
大臣法小臣廉官職相序君臣相正國之
肥也
束帛加璧往德也
暴民不作諸侯賓服兵革不試五刑不用
百姓無患天子不怒如此則樂達矣
升車則有鸞和之音
第貳場
論
punctuated:
遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。僖公四年。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。襄公十一年。夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。昭公四年。
宋公伐邾。昭公十九年。夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。昭公二十年。

禮記
大臣法，小臣廉，官職相序，君臣相正，國之肥也。
束帛加璧，往德也。
暴民不作，諸侯賓服，兵革不試，五刑不用，百姓無患，天子不怒，如此則樂達矣。
升車則有鸞和之音。

第貳場
論
translation_en:
They thereupon invaded Chu and halted at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and made a covenant at Shaoling (4th year of Duke Xi). The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang the Heir Apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in invading Zheng; they met at Xiaoyu (11th year of Duke Xiang). In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, Zuo the Heir Apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen (4th year of Duke Zhao).
The Duke of Song invaded Zhu (19th year of Duke Zhao). In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song (20th year of Duke Zhao).

Record of Rites (Liji)
When the great ministers are law-abiding, the lesser ministers are incorrupt, official duties are kept in due order, and ruler and ministers rectify one another, that is the thriving abundance of a state.
Bundles of silk topped with jade disks are presented to convey virtue.
Violent people do not arise, the feudal lords submit as guests, weapons and armor are not put to use, the five punishments are not employed, the common people have no distress, and the Son of Heaven has no occasion for anger: when it is like this, then music has reached everywhere.
When ascending the carriage, there is the sound of the luan and he bells.

Second Session
Discourse

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
咸言鑿鑿近道也唐虞三代邈不可尚
自漢而下英君繼作中間謹畏天戒軫
念人窮者炳烺史冊歷可玫鏡不識於
古帝王之道亦有彷彿其萬一者與洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝受命開基
成祖文皇帝嗣統綏化其祗承
明命與夫籌畫區寓之實載在
政要諸書者可覩也
===
列聖相承授受一道迨我
皇上躬操神明
嗣登大寶十載于茲所以奉若
天道子惠困窮者固足以衍億萬載無疆之福
矣邇者星象垂異四方水旱屢
奏公車乃
上下禱祀齋居減膳蠲逋賑匱視昔有加且
勑諭臣工共圖修省是其敬
天勤民之心眞有遠紹
punctuated: 咸言鑿鑿近道也。唐虞三代，邈不可尚。自漢而下，英君繼作，中間謹畏天戒、軫念人窮者，炳烺史冊，歷可玫鏡。不識於古帝王之道，亦有彷彿其萬一者與？洪惟我太祖高皇帝受命開基，成祖文皇帝嗣統綏化，其祗承明命，與夫籌畫區寓之實，載在《政要》諸書者，可覩也。列聖相承，授受一道。迨我皇上躬操神明，嗣登大寶，十載于茲，所以奉若天道、子惠困窮者，固足以衍億萬載無疆之福矣。邇者星象垂異，四方水旱屢奏公車，乃上下禱祀，齋居減膳，蠲逋賑匱，視昔有加；且勑諭臣工，共圖修省。是其敬天勤民之心，眞有遠紹
translation_en:
…all speak with well-grounded certainty, approaching the Way. The eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties are distant and unsurpassed. From the Han dynasty onward, heroic rulers arose in succession; among them, those who cautiously heeded the warnings of Heaven and felt deep compassion for the distress of the people shine brightly in the historical annals, each verifiable as a mirror for reflection [?]. Yet one wonders whether, in relation to the Way of the ancient emperors and kings, they attained even a ten-thousandth part of a resemblance to it?

Reflecting grandly upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), who received the Mandate and laid the foundation, and our Accomplished Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Chengzu), who succeeded to the line and pacified and transformed the realm: the realities of how they reverently upheld the Bright Mandate and planned for the empire within its boundaries can be seen recorded in the Essentials of Government (Zhengyao) and other books. The successive sage emperors inherited the realm from one another, transmitting and receiving a single Way. Coming down to Our reigning Emperor: personally wielding godlike intelligence, He succeeded to and ascended the Great Treasure, and ten years have passed until now. The means by which He complies with the Way of Heaven and treats the distressed and impoverished with parental kindness are indeed sufficient to extend boundless blessings for hundreds of millions of years. Recently, astral phenomena have displayed anomalies, and floods and droughts from the four quarters have been repeatedly reported in memorials to the throne. Thereupon, sacrifices and prayers have been offered above and below; He has dwelt in fasting and reduced His imperial meals, remitted tax arrears and relieved the destitute, doing even more than in the past. Moreover, He has issued imperial commands instructing His officials to jointly plan for self-cultivation and reflection. Thus, His mind that reveres Heaven and labors diligently for the people truly reaches far back to continue…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
帝王近述
祖宗而陋漢唐宋于不足言者亦可敬陳其一
二歟又不知應
天以實中外百司將何以仰荅
宸衷以爲
上下承休之助爾多士固效用有日者願盡言
之其勿讓
問文章之作所以經世帝王之文載在六
籍當時臯夔伊傅相與謨謀于廟堂初
===
不言文而吐辭爲經垂憲萬古蓋政與
學未相析也自戰國以來天下馳騖于
戰功儒術既絀獨齊魯之間學者不廢
於是始有以經生稱若申培公濟南伏
生之流者焉而政與學析爲二矣司馬
遷班固各有儒林循吏傳而范曄之作
後漢書又分儒林文苑二傳業儒者務
經術業文者尚贍博是學者又自相析
而與政事爲三也魏晉以來崇飾浮競
punctuated:
帝王，近述祖宗，而陋漢、唐、宋于不足言者，亦可敬陳其一二歟？又不知應天以實，中外百司將何以仰荅宸衷，以爲上下承休之助？爾多士固效用有日者，願盡言之，其勿讓。

問：文章之作，所以經世。帝王之文，載在六籍。當時臯、夔、伊、傅，相與謨謀于廟堂，初不言文，而吐辭爲經，垂憲萬古，蓋政與學未相析也。自戰國以來，天下馳騖于戰功，儒術既絀，獨齊、魯之間，學者不廢，於是始有以經生稱，若申培公、濟南伏生之流者焉，而政與學析爲二矣。司馬遷、班固各有《儒林》、《循吏》傳，而范曄之作《後漢書》，又分《儒林》、《文苑》二傳。業儒者務經術，業文者尚贍博，是學者又自相析，而與政事爲三也。魏、晉以來，崇飾浮競，
translation_en:
… the sage Emperors and Kings of antiquity and closely carries forward the legacy of our Imperial Ancestors, rendering the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties too paltry even to mention! May you respectfully set forth one or two points concerning this? Furthermore, in responding to Heaven with substantive action, how shall the myriad officials at court and in the provinces respectfully answer His Majesty's heartfelt concern, so as to assist both sovereign and subjects in receiving Heaven's blessings? You many scholars will surely have a day when you render service to the state; I wish you to speak fully and without hesitation.

Question: The composition of literary writings is the means by which to order the world. The writings of the ancient Emperors and Kings are recorded in the Six Classics. At that time, Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue deliberated together over counsels and plans in the ancestral temple and court; they never spoke initially of "literature" as such, yet the words they uttered became classics that handed down models for ten thousand ages, because governance and learning had not yet been separated from one another. From the Warring States period onward, the world galloped in pursuit of military achievements and Confucian arts were sidelined; only in the region of Qi and Lu did scholars not abandon them. Thus there first began to be those known as "scholars of the Classics" (jingsheng), such as Master Shen Pei (Shen Peigong) and Master Fu of Jinan (Jinan Fusheng), and governance and learning were split into two. Sima Qian and Ban Gu each included separate biographies of "Confucian Scholars" (Rulin) and "Upright Officials" (Xunli) in their histories, while Fan Ye, in compiling the Book of the Later Han (Hou Han shu), further divided scholarship into the two biographical chapters of "Confucian Scholars" (Rulin) and "Literary Men" (Wenyuan). Those who pursued Confucian scholarship devoted themselves to classical exegesis, whereas those who pursued literature prized rich erudition; thus scholars further split among themselves, forming three distinct realms alongside governance. From the Wei and Jin dynasties onward, people esteemed ornate artifice and superficial rivalry, …

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
祖述虛玄陵夷至於梁陳之綺靡文儒
之業幾墜于地唐興而陳子昂李白力
追古詩韓愈氏力追古文自是詩文始
各有擅長者而文苑之中又相析矣曾
王歐蘇衍韓氏之流者也至周程張朱
出而皆以土苴視之自今觀之韓歐之
徒豈盡無一言幾于道者與今之學儒
者稱程朱學文者稱史漢學詩者稱盛
唐各就其質所近而終不如古人者何
與其出而應世亦有俾于治理者否諸
士必有心知其意者其究言之
===
問古之成大事者于簿書期會之間不甚
過人惟投艱應猝而後才始見遵何道
也古人取人專在識量識欲遠而量欲
大成大事者以此安用剞劂小才哉然
識量果何以辨嘗觀古人有以㱕㞉能
任而知其克秦者有以蒲博必得而知
其克蜀者有目瑯琊總角而知其必誤
punctuated:
祖述虛玄，陵夷至於梁、陳之綺靡，文儒之業幾墜于地。唐興，而陳子昂、李白力追古詩，韓愈氏力追古文，自是詩、文始各有擅長者，而《文苑》之中又相析矣。曾、王、歐、蘇，衍韓氏之流者也；至周、程、張、朱出，而皆以土苴視之。自今觀之，韓、歐之徒，豈盡無一言幾于道者與？今之學儒者稱程、朱，學文者稱《史》、《漢》，學詩者稱盛唐，各就其質所近，而終不如古人者，何與？其出而應世，亦有俾于治理者否？諸士必有心知其意者，其究言之。

問：古之成大事者，于簿書期會之間不甚過人，惟投艱應猝而後才始見，遵何道也？古人取人，專在識量，識欲遠而量欲大，成大事者以此，安用剞劂小才哉？然識量果何以辨？嘗觀古人有以㱕㞉能任而知其克秦者，有以蒲博必得而知其克蜀者，有目瑯琊總角而知其必誤
translation_en:
… modeled themselves on emptiness and mystery, declining further into the ornate frivolity of the Liang and Chen dynasties, until the enterprise of literary and Confucian scholarship nearly fell to the ground. When the Tang arose, Chen Zi'ang 陳子昂 and Li Bai 李白 strove to recover ancient-style poetry, while Han Yu 韓愈 strove to recover ancient-style prose. From this point on, poetry and prose each began to have their own specialists, and within the "Literary Garden" itself a further division emerged. Zeng Gong 曾鞏, Wang Anshi 王安石, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修, and Su Shi 蘇軾 were those who carried on the current of Han Yu; yet when Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers 程 (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤), Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 appeared, they regarded all of them as mere dregs and refuse. Viewed from the present, among figures like Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu, could it really be that they had not a single word that approached the Way? Today, those who study Confucian learning invoke Cheng and Zhu, those who study prose invoke the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the History of the Former Han (Hanshu), and those who study poetry invoke the High Tang; each follows what is closest to his own natural disposition, yet in the end they do not equal the ancients—why is this? And when they go forth to respond to the needs of the world, are they of any aid to governance and order or not? You gentlemen must surely be ones who understand the meaning of this in your hearts; set it forth in full.

Question: Those in antiquity who accomplished great deeds did not much surpass others amid routine account books and scheduled meetings; only when cast into hardship and responding to sudden crises did their talent become manifest. What principle did they follow? When the ancients selected men, they focused exclusively on insight and capacity: insight they wished to be far-reaching, and capacity they wished to be vast. It was by these that men accomplished great deeds—what use had they for the petty talents of a chisel and carving knife? Yet how indeed are insight and capacity to be discerned? I have observed that among the ancients, there was one who knew from how a man wore his clogs [?] and bore his duties that he would defeat Former Qin; there was one who knew from a man's determination to win at dice that he would conquer Shu; there was one who, upon seeing a youth of Langye with his hair still bound in tufts, knew that he would surely ruin…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
蒼生者有見范陽偏校而知其必亂幽
州者有於石晉開創之初而論郡國無
備之患者有于慶曆治平之際而論汴
都四戰之危者當時或未信及質之後
如持劵何其明與有沉海浪涌而吟嘯
不言人審其鎮安朝野者有走馬突出
而神色不動人決其必爲公輔者有發
匕首于臥内而執枕自如者有竊銀器
于帳外而熟視不語者有于朝堂見詆
===
而不詢姓名者有爲諫官被論而反薦
其父子者其人度量與世何懸絶假令
局曲者當之亦能然與夫大匠不斵大
庖不豆小謹者不大立餐食者不肥體
豪傑之士安可以簿書期會程也此必
有本焉諸士如慕效之其明著所由
問古之取士未甞有方或取於屠販或取
於讎虜管夷吾之相齊穆公之霸秦皆
然唐宋以後拘泥資格自科目而外鮮
punctuated:
蒼生者，有見范陽偏校而知其必亂幽州者，有於石晉開創之初而論郡國無備之患者，有于慶曆、治平之際而論汴都四戰之危者。當時或未信，及質之後，如持劵，何其明與？有汎海浪涌而吟嘯不言，人審其鎮安朝野者；有走馬突出而神色不動，人決其必爲公輔者；有發匕首于臥内而執枕自如者；有竊銀器于帳外而熟視不語者；有于朝堂見詆而不詢姓名者；有爲諫官被論而反薦其父子者。其人度量與世何懸絶！假令局曲者當之，亦能然與？夫大匠不斵，大庖不豆，小謹者不大立，餐食者不肥體，豪傑之士，安可以簿書期會程也？此必有本焉，諸士如慕效之，其明著所由。

問：古之取士，未甞有方，或取於屠販，或取於讎虜，管夷吾之相齊，穆公之霸秦，皆然。唐、宋以後，拘泥資格，自科目而外，鮮
translation_en:
… the common people; some saw a subordinate officer in Fanyang and knew that he would surely bring rebellion to Youzhou; some, at the very founding of the Shi Jin dynasty, discussed the peril of the commanderies and principalities being unprepared; and some, during the Qingli (1041–1048) and Zhiping (1064–1067) eras, discussed the danger of the capital at Bian being exposed to warfare on all four sides. At the time, people might not have believed them, yet when verified against later events, their words proved as certain as holding a tally—how prescient they were! Some, when waves surged as they sailed the sea, chanted and whistled without saying a word, from which people judged that they would calm and stabilize court and country; some, when a galloping horse suddenly bolted out before them, showed no change of expression, from which people determined that they would surely become Dukes or Ministers; some, when a dagger was drawn in their bedchamber, held their pillow with complete composure; some, when silver vessels were being stolen from outside their curtains, watched closely without speaking; some, when slandered in the court hall, did not even ask the detractor's name; and some, when impeached by a Censor, instead recommended both him and his son. How vastly their magnanimity surpassed that of the common world! Suppose men of narrow and cramped minds were put in their place—could they have acted thus? Now, a master carpenter does not hew, and a master cook does not arrange the serving vessels; those who are fastidious about petty matters do not achieve great standing, and those who nibble at their food [?] do not fatten their bodies. How can heroic and outstanding men be measured by account books and administrative deadlines? There must be a fundamental basis for this. If you gentlemen admire and wish to emulate them, set forth clearly from what it arises.

Question: In antiquity, the selection of men of service was never confined to a single method. Some were chosen from among butchers and peddlers, and some from among enemies and captives; Guan Yiwu (Guan Zhong 管仲) serving as chief minister of Qi, and Duke Mu achieving hegemony in秦 (Qin), were both examples of this. From the Tang and Song dynasties onward, governance has been bound by qualifications and seniority, and outside the civil service examination categories, few…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
得進者顧其得人之效孰盛漢平津樂
安號爲儒宗卒不能爲漢立不世大功
而趙廣漢尹翁歸張敞王尊皆起於吏
胥乃能卓絶俊偉震耀四海豈務章句
者之不如習法律耶抑上之人鼓舞之
使得自奮也夫人固有才智奇絶而不
能爲章句者茍一之以制科是使奇才
絶智有時而窮也近者
廟堂屢下
===
詔令吏部三途竝用然卒不能大破拘攣之習
而倜儻度外之士在制舉外亦鮮見豈
古與今異非常之原不可施設與抑鼓
舞未盡與諸士有槩於中其詳著以對
問管子有云夫兵古今莫能廢也我
祖宗兵制
令甲詳矣軍有屯者有技擊者以屯養技擊
古者寓兵于農意也昇平日久軍政寖
弛弱者竄而强者亢乃有振武新營之
punctuated:
得進者。顧其得人之效，孰盛？漢平津、樂安，號爲儒宗，卒不能爲漢立不世大功；而趙廣漢、尹翁歸、張敞、王尊，皆起於吏胥，乃能卓絶俊偉，震耀四海。豈務章句者之不如習法律耶？抑上之人鼓舞之，使得自奮也？夫人固有才智奇絶而不能爲章句者，茍一之以制科，是使奇才絶智有時而窮也。近者廟堂屢下詔，令吏部三途竝用，然卒不能大破拘攣之習，而倜儻度外之士，在制舉外亦鮮見。豈古與今異，非常之原不可施設與？抑鼓舞未盡與？諸士有槩於中，其詳著以對。
問：管子有云：「夫兵，古今莫能廢也。」我祖宗兵制，令甲詳矣。軍有屯者，有技擊者，以屯養技擊，古者寓兵于農意也。昇平日久，軍政寖弛，弱者竄而强者亢，乃有振武新營之
translation_en:
… were able to advance. Yet if we consider the efficacy in obtaining men of talent, which period was more flourishing? In the Han dynasty, the Marquis of Pingjin (Gongsun Hong 公孫弘) and the Marquis of Le'an (Kuang Heng 匡衡) were acclaimed as models of Confucian scholarship, yet in the end they could not establish extraordinary, epoch-making achievements for the Han; whereas Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢, Yin Wenggui 尹翁歸, Zhang Chang 張敞, and Wang Zun 王尊 all rose from the ranks of lesser clerks and subofficial functionaries, and yet were able to be outstanding and brilliant, shaking and dazzling all within the Four Seas. Is it that those who devote themselves to textual exegesis are inferior to those versed in laws and statutes? Or is it that those above inspired and roused them so that they could exert themselves? Truly, there are men who possess extraordinary talent and wisdom yet are incapable of textual exegesis; if we uniformly restrict recruitment to the regular civil service examinations, this will cause men of extraordinary talent and surpassing wisdom at times to be left without an avenue. Recently, the court has repeatedly handed down edicts ordering the Ministry of Personnel to employ men through all three qualification paths concurrently. Yet in the end it has been unable to break through the habit of rigid adherence to convention, and unconventional men of exceptional caliber outside the examination system are rarely seen. Is it that antiquity and the present are different, so that extraordinary foundations cannot be put into practice? Or is it that our encouragement and stimulation have not yet been exhausted? Gentlemen, as you hold convictions on this in your hearts, set them forth in detail in your replies.

Question: Master Guan (Guanzi 管子) said: "As for arms and soldiers, neither antiquity nor the present has been able to dispense with them." The military system of our Imperial Ancestors is set forth in full detail in the statutory codes. Among the hereditary military forces, there are state-farm troops and there are combat troops; using the state farms to support the combat troops embodies the ancient intention of lodging soldiers among the peasantry. As peace has lasted for a long time, military administration has gradually grown lax; the weak flee while the strong grow recalcitrant, which has led to the mutiny of the Zhenwu New Camp…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
變有雲中之叛譚者遂嘆軍不足恃而
紛紛議兵矣機兵弊而議客兵客兵弊
而議土著此數者果無裨軍制乎比年
閩浙有事島夷寔用以勝而近日一二
跳梁者又出於兵弊所必至視軍何異
哉且兵多則多制餉將多則多制祿民
患益賦而衛所原屯日入漁獵是兵與
軍兩相病矣貴筑抗制苗夷衛所錯置
自昔爲用惟是尺籍之軍而已然消耗
===
者什八老弱者什五卽各哨兵亦俱以
苗仲充虛數焉有如一旦事出叵測計
將安出耶其亦可預資於召募耶夫地
遠則募難民瘠則餉難貴之屯租已不
足給軍之半卽近日省城募兵千名而
贖鍰亦竭矣意者因地通變他或有良
筴歟或謂科糧無差人易影射議於其
中量起丁役以塞弊孔而佐軍伍其說
亦可行歟諸士生長於斯當必籌之審
punctuated: 變，有雲中之叛。譚者遂嘆軍不足恃，而紛紛議兵矣。機兵弊而議客兵，客兵弊而議土著，此數者果無裨軍制乎？比年閩、浙有事島夷，寔用以勝；而近日一二跳梁者，又出於兵。弊所必至，視軍何異哉！且兵多則多制餉，將多則多制祿，民患益賦，而衛所原屯日入漁獵，是兵與軍兩相病矣。貴筑抗制苗夷，衛所錯置，自昔爲用，惟是尺籍之軍而已。然消耗者什八，老弱者什五，卽各哨兵亦俱以苗、仲充虛數焉。有如一旦事出叵測，計將安出耶？其亦可預資於召募耶？夫地遠則募難，民瘠則餉難。貴之屯租已不足給軍之半，卽近日省城募兵千名，而贖鍰亦竭矣。意者因地通變，他或有良筴歟？或謂科糧無差，人易影射，議於其中量起丁役，以塞弊孔而佐軍伍，其說亦可行歟？諸士生長於斯，當必籌之審
translation_en: … mutiny, and the rebellion in Yunzhong. Commentators consequently lamented that the hereditary military (jun 軍) could not be relied upon, and one after another they debated non-hereditary troops (bing 兵). When the militia troops (jibing 機兵) fell into abuse, they proposed guest troops (kebing 客兵); when guest troops fell into abuse, they proposed local recruits (tuzhu 土著). Are these several options truly of no benefit to the military system? In recent years, when Fujian and Zhejiang had trouble with the island barbarians, they actually used such troops to achieve victory; yet recently, one or two cases of unruly defiance have again arisen from among the recruited troops. When abuses reach their inevitable outcome, how do they differ from the hereditary military! Furthermore, when recruited troops are numerous, more provisions must be established for them; when commanders are numerous, more salaries must be established for them. The common people suffer from increased taxes, while the original military colony lands (tun 屯) of the Guards and Battalions (weisuo 衛所) daily fall prey to predatory seizure—thus the recruited troops and the hereditary military mutually harm one another. Guizhu [Guizhou] resists and holds in check the Miao and Yi peoples, with Guards and Battalions interspersed throughout. Since antiquity, those employed have solely been the hereditary soldiers on the military registers. Yet eight out of ten have been lost to attrition, and five out of ten are old and weak; even the troops at the various outposts (shao 哨) are all filled out in nominal numbers by Miao and Zhongjia people. Suppose one day an unforeseen crisis occurs—from where will a plan be devised? Can we also rely in advance on recruitment? Now, because the region is remote, recruitment is difficult; because the people are impoverished, provisioning is difficult. The military colony rents of Guizhou are already insufficient to supply half the hereditary soldiers, and when the provincial capital recently recruited a thousand soldiers, the redemption fees (shuhuan 贖鍰) were also exhausted. Could it be that by adapting to local conditions, there might be some other sound strategy? Some say that because grain tax assessment carries no corvée labor (cha 差), people easily engage in fraudulent evasion (yingshe 影射), and they propose proportionally levying adult male labor service (dingyi 丁役) from among them in order to plug the loopholes of abuse and assist the military ranks—is this theory also feasible? You gentlemen were born and raised here and have surely deliberated on this thoroughly …
