punctuated: 時也，不圖治軍而徒求兵於召募，是置其子而反育人之子也；不圖治屯而徒需食於贖鍰，是財貸於人而反假人之財也，又惟之甚也。今之軍伍半折，丁壯阻消，爲宜詳覈所部，悉清勾之，使原伍漸還，名不浮籍；而又嚴逋逃之禁，重督遲司，譏關出入，毋令以賄脫伍者。如是則軍復矣。夫貴雖僻壤，置衞十八，各戍千餘，誠得盡勾，數萬之衆在也，何憂兵寡？今之屯田虛冒，悉入豪右，爲宜大索侵沒，董以重法，必歸之軍，無論賦盈；而又嚴課耕之令，督之總管，別勤惰而考成焉。如是則屯復矣。夫貴雖瘠土，而屯多膏田，衞各若干，誠得盡種，九年之蓄在也，何患食匱？或者謂勾軍必假於緩期，而抽丁可議以爲助。貴之墾田科糧而無差，有差之糧率資以影射。玆欲量其糧而起丁役，既足以塞弊孔，時而訓練之，又足以佐軍伍，此固一策也。或者謂與其
translation_en: …time, not planning to put the regular military (jun) in order while merely seeking hired troops (bing) through recruitment is like setting aside one's own son only to raise someone else's son; not planning to put the military colonies (tun) in order while merely relying for food on redemption fines is like lending one's wealth to others only to borrow someone else's wealth—this too is extreme folly [?惟, likely for 怪 or 謬]. Today, the military ranks are depleted by half and able-bodied men have dwindled away. It is fitting to carefully verify those under jurisdiction and thoroughly clear out the registers to conscript replacements (qinggou), causing the original ranks to gradually be restored so that names do not merely float on the registers; and furthermore, to tighten the prohibitions against desertion, heavily hold accountable the officials in charge of tracking [?遲司, likely 緝司], and inspect those passing in and out of the checkpoints, not allowing anyone to escape the ranks through bribery. If this is done, then the regular military will be restored. Now, although Guizhou is a remote region, eighteen Guards (wei) have been established, each garrisoned by over a thousand men. If indeed all can be conscripted back, a multitude of several tens of thousands will be right there—what worry would there be of a shortage of soldiers? Today, the military colony lands (tuntian) are falsely claimed and have entirely fallen into the hands of powerful families. It is fitting to conduct a sweeping search for encroached and confiscated lands, supervise the matter with severe laws, and insist on returning them to the military regardless of whether the tax quota is already full; and furthermore, to tighten the orders for assessing cultivation, supervise this through the colony managers (zongguan), and distinguish between the diligent and the indolent to evaluate their performance. If this is done, then the military colonies will be restored. Now, although Guizhou has barren soil, the military colonies have many fertile fields, with each Guard possessing a certain amount. If indeed all can be planted, nine years' worth of reserves will be right there—what fear would there be of a shortage of food? Some say that conscripting replacement soldiers necessarily requires granting an extended period of time, whereas levying able-bodied men (chouding) can be discussed as an aid. In Guizhou, newly reclaimed fields are assessed for grain tax without labor service (chai), and grain lands that do bear labor service frequently use this for tax evasion by fraudulent registration (yingshe). Now, if one wishes to measure their grain tax and raise labor service from able-bodied men accordingly, this will not only suffice to plug the loopholes of corruption, but if we train them at regular intervals, it will also suffice to assist the military ranks. This is certainly one strategy. Some say that rather than…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
士之心故士無死綏之志力竭於供作而
食耗於侵漁居恒懼者不得權貪者不得
豐臨敵安得同心之士斯於長上蔑如矣
其於練氣練心又安在哉是故撫之貴以
其道也淮陰驅市人以戰所嚮披靡者誠
不慮夫無兵而慮無將兵者也夫天下事
若奕棋然舉而不定不勝其耦故愚願當
事者亟復
祖宗不易之規而毋襲召募權宜之計一意練
===
軍治屯清覈當確督率當嚴侵牟者當治
漁獵者當懲而又馭之以良帥董之以重
臣蒐苗視乎先王封場飭於軍國虎旅林
立葵藿不揉之勢在焉北禦虜南備夷持
此筴而往矣幺麼諸苗夫何患乎跛者雖
不能行然善譚慶忌之捷求捷者惡可廢
之愚言猶足以方於此惟執事者圖之
punctuated: 士之心，故士無死綏之志。力竭於供作，而食耗於侵漁。居恒懼者不得權，貪者不得豐，臨敵安得同心之士？斯於長上蔑如矣，其於練氣、練心又安在哉？是故撫之貴以其道也。淮陰驅市人以戰，所嚮披靡者，誠不慮夫無兵，而慮無將兵者也。夫天下事若奕棋然，舉而不定，不勝其耦。故愚願當事者亟復祖宗不易之規，而毋襲召募權宜之計。一意練軍治屯，清覈當確，督率當嚴，侵牟者當治，漁獵者當懲；而又馭之以良帥，董之以重臣。蒐苗視乎先王，封場飭於軍國。虎旅林立，葵藿不揉之勢在焉。北禦虜，南備夷，持此筴而往矣，幺麼諸苗，夫何患乎？跛者雖不能行，然善譚慶忌之捷，求捷者惡可廢之？愚言猶足以方於此，惟執事者圖之。
translation_en:
… the hearts of the soldiers, and thus the soldiers lack the resolve to die at their posts. Their strength is exhausted by menial labor and corvée, while their rations are depleted by embezzlement and predation. In ordinary times, the fearful fail to gain authority [or perhaps: those who fear the law do not get their due? / the timid cannot weigh matters?], and the greedy are never satisfied [or: cannot be satiated]; when facing the enemy, how then can one obtain soldiers of a single heart and mind? Thus they hold their superiors in utter contempt; where, then, is the training of their vital spirit and the training of their minds? Therefore, in pacifying and caring for them, what is valued is doing so according to the proper Way. When the Marquis of Huaiyin (Han Xin 韓信) drove marketplace folk into battle and swept away all before him, it was truly because he did not worry about lacking soldiers, but worried about lacking someone capable of commanding soldiers.

Now, the affairs of the world are like a game of chess: if one makes moves without a settled strategy, one cannot defeat one's opponent. Therefore, I愚 (your humble candidate) wish that those in authority would urgently restore the immutable regulations of the Imperial Ancestors, and stop following the expedient scheme of recruiting mercenaries. Wholeheartedly train the hereditary military and manage the military farms (tuntian); clearing the registers and verification must be accurate, supervision and leadership must be strict, those who encroach and profiteer must be punished, and those who prey upon the troops must be chastised. Moreover, command them with fine generals and oversee them with senior ministers. Conduct the spring and summer military reviews (sou and miao) on the model of the former kings, and keep the frontiers in strict order for the military and the state. With tiger-like troops standing thick as a forest, the posture of rendering wild weeds unplucked [i.e., an inviolable, awe-inspiring presence like the猛虎 on the mountain protecting the flora] will be present therein. To defend against the northern caitiffs in the north and guard against the southern barbarians in the south, one need only hold to this strategy and go forth—as for the petty and insignificant Miao tribes, what cause for worry could they be?

Although a lame man cannot walk, he can speak well of the swiftness of Qing Ji (慶忌); how can one who seeks swiftness discard his words? My humble words may still be compared to this; I only pray that Your Excellency will consider them.

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄後序
譚者曰造化神奇鍾于豐壤
而洩于人地湫阨則弗炳靈
非茂異所躔綜其實不然惟
上作之爾有以作之則聲應氣求
自相鼓舞若日有人程督其
間者此惟其人惟其時而地
===
靈弗與焉蓋自昔茂異之域
紱冕所興者在虞夏之際三
河爲卓犖迨文武興則羣于
陝洛孔孟作則羣于鄒魯漢
之盛也經術節義東西二京
懸衡焉自唐以來而吳楚閩
粤遭離不一文獻代爲雌雄
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄後序

譚者曰：「造化神奇，鍾于豐壤而洩于人；地湫阨則弗炳靈，非茂異所躔。」綜其實不然，惟上作之爾。有以作之，則聲應氣求，自相鼓舞，若日有人程督其間者。此惟其人，惟其時，而地靈弗與焉。蓋自昔茂異之域，紱冕所興者，在虞、夏之際，三河爲卓犖；迨文、武興，則羣于陝、洛；孔、孟作，則羣于鄒、魯。漢之盛也，經術節義，東、西二京懸衡焉。自唐以來，而吳、楚、閩、粤遭離不一，文獻代爲雌雄，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

Commentators say: "The wondrous power of nature concentrates in fertile soil and manifests itself in human beings; where the land is low and cramped, it does not shine forth with numinous spirit, nor is it a place frequented by flourishing and extraordinary talent." Yet when we examine the reality comprehensively, it is not so; it depends solely on how those above stimulate them. If there is a means to stimulate them, then like sounds respond to one another and kindred spirits seek each other out, inspiring and encouraging one another of their own accord, as though someone were supervising and urging them on day by day. This depends solely on the people and solely on the times, while the spirit of the land has no part in it. Indeed, among the regions of flourishing and extraordinary talent since antiquity, where ceremonial sashes and caps of office arose: during the eras of Yu and Xia, the Three Rivers region was preeminent; when Kings Wen and Wu arose, talent gathered in Shaan and Luo; when Confucius and Mencius appeared, it gathered in Zou and Lu. At the height of the Han dynasty, in classical scholarship and moral integrity, the Eastern and Western Capitals held the balance. From the Tang dynasty onward, Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue encountered varying fortunes, and in culture and learning they took turns vying for supremacy. …

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
地靈何常哉我
太祖初掃雰雺基自江介故翼軫
之野藻絢首盛歷紀臻茲風
美所扇昭天漏泉卽遐闊晻
昧咸能殷薦厥心冀稱
明德矧惟黔中麗于
神州泳沫最夂者乎
===
列聖相繼咸以道德仁義霑濡而
浸潤之無牂牁僰道之使無
勞深靡莫之師葉楡以南五
溪以西方領習矩步者委它
乎其中橫經而述堯舜周孔
如述其先世我
皇上臨御循虞道之鬱滯數下
punctuated: 地靈何常哉？我太祖初掃雰雺，基自江介，故翼軫之野，藻絢首盛。歷紀臻茲，風美所扇，昭天漏泉，卽遐闊晻昧，咸能殷薦厥心，冀稱明德，矧惟黔中麗于神州，泳沫最夂者乎！列聖相繼，咸以道德仁義霑濡而浸潤之。無牂牁、僰道之使，無勞深、靡莫之師，葉楡以南、五溪以西，方領習矩步者，委它乎其中，橫經而述堯、舜、周、孔，如述其先世。我皇上臨御，循虞道之鬱滯，數下
translation_en: How could the spiritual vitality of a land be constant? When our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) first swept away the dark mists, he laid his foundations along the Yangzi River; therefore, in the regions corresponding to the Yi and Zhen constellations, literary brilliance was the first to flourish. Through successive reigns down to the present, fanned by the beauty of our customs, this influence has shone across the heavens and seeped into the deepest springs. Even in distant, remote, and obscure lands, all are able to ardently offer up their hearts in hopes of matching His illustrious virtue—how much more so for Qianzhong (Guizhou), which is attached to the Divine Land (China) and has been bathed in its grace for the longest time! The successive Sage Emperors followed one another, all moistening and saturating the land with morality, humanity, and righteousness. Without needing envoys sent to Zangke and Bodao, and without needing armies marched against Laoshen and Mimo, south of Yeyu and west of the Five Streams (Wuxi), scholars wearing square-collared robes and practicing measured steps move with poised grace in their midst, holding the Classics across their laps and recounting the ways of Yao, Shun, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius as if recounting their own ancestors. Since Our August Emperor ascended the throne, showing concern for any stagnation or obstruction of the Way, he has repeatedly handed down…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
詔書深懲彫蔚嘉與宇内之士臻
于正學至精所動若元氣及
物馳傳鶩置莫先焉以故諸
士子雖越在萬里外罔不濯
慮竦神悅而承流如在
輦轂之側而瞻依
日月也蓋虞夏成周之際英賢所
===
產僅盛于三河陜洛都會之
間而我
明際天極地光被六幽無不效
其靈秀嗚呼盛矣不佞之被
聘來也入疆而觀其士民其
狀脜然不儇入棘而閲其文
則咸能潤色六學旁及諸史
punctuated: 詔書，深懲彫蔚，嘉與宇内之士臻于正學。至精所動，若元氣及物，馳傳鶩置莫先焉。以故諸士子雖越在萬里外，罔不濯慮竦神，悅而承流，如在輦轂之側而瞻依日月也。蓋虞、夏、成周之際，英賢所產，僅盛于三河、陜、洛都會之間；而我明際天極地，光被六幽，無不效其靈秀。嗚呼，盛矣！不佞之被聘來也，入疆而觀其士民，其狀脜然不儇；入棘而閲其文，則咸能潤色六學，旁及諸史，
translation_en: …edicts, deeply admonishing ornate and florid writing, and graciously encouraging scholars throughout the realm to attain orthodox learning. That which is stirred by His utmost essence is like the primordial vital breath reaching all things—even express couriers and galloping post-horses cannot outpace it. For this reason, although the examination candidates are located ten thousand li away, there are none who do not cleanse their thoughts and rouse their spirits, gladly embracing the current of transformation, as though they were beside the imperial chariot and gazing up in reliance upon the sun and moon. Indeed, during the eras of Yu, Xia, and Chengzhou, the production of outstanding worthies flourished only among the metropolitan centers of the Three Rivers, Shaan, and Luo; whereas our Ming dynasty reaches to the ends of heaven and earth, its radiance covering the six remote directions, so that there is no place that does not offer up its spiritual excellence. Oh, how magnificent! When I, lacking in talent, was invited to come here, upon entering the territory and observing its scholars and commoners, their demeanor was honest and unpretentious [? 脜然不儇]; upon entering the examination compound and reviewing their essays, all were able to embellish the Six Teachings and extend laterally to the various histories,…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
藻不彫樸華不變淳駸駸埒
中原矣夫銅鼓木閣之峯非
增秀也來鳫洗馬之泉非增
深也而一時人文其流彌暢
豈非有以作之而聲氣自相
鼓舞與故曰惟其人惟其時
而地靈弗與也繼先又聞之
===
人情貴耳而賤目先聲而後
實良驥不擇地而產而世以
爲必華山之騄耳而後行遠
者泥于常也屬者黔之諸士
學者牛毛而成者麟角也故
千里一士以爲比肩不得與
中原頡頏今異矣然或中原
punctuated: 藻不彫樸，華不變淳，駸駸埒中原矣。夫銅鼓、木閣之峯非增秀也，來鳫、洗馬之泉非增深也，而一時人文，其流彌暢，豈非有以作之，而聲氣自相鼓舞與？故曰：惟其人，惟其時，而地靈弗與也。繼先又聞之：人情貴耳而賤目，先聲而後實。良驥不擇地而產，而世以爲必華山之騄耳而後行遠者，泥于常也。屬者黔之諸士，學者牛毛，而成者麟角也。故千里一士，以爲比肩，不得與中原頡頏。今異矣，然或中原
translation_en:
…their ornate diction does not carve away simplicity, and their brilliance does not alter their purity; they are rapidly coming to rival the Central Plains. Now, the peaks of Tonggu 銅鼓 and Muge 木閣 have not grown any moresplendid, nor have the springs of Laiyan 來鳫 and Xima 洗馬 grown any deeper, yet the literary culture of this generation flows ever more freely. Is it not because there has been something to rouse it, so that kindred spirits naturally inspire one another? Thus it is said: it depends only on the men and only on the times; the numinous power of the land plays no part in it.

I, Jixian 繼先, have also heard it said that human nature prizes what is heard by the ear and slights what is seen by the eye, putting reputation first and substance second. Fine steeds do not choose the land where they are born, yet the world supposes that a horse must be a Lu'er 騄耳 from Mount Hua 華山 before it can travel far—this is being bound by convention. Previously, among the scholars of Qian 黔 [Guizhou], those who studied were as numerous as ox hairs, while those who succeeded were as rare as unicorn horns. Therefore, if one scholar appeared in a thousand li, people considered them to be standing shoulder to shoulder, yet they could not contend as equals with the Central Plains. Today it is different. Yet perhaps when a scholar from the Central Plains…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之士釋荷而來也少自適上
則以繡緣繡而以素緣素其
懿灼然黔士之用于世也少
不力則獨行衆指獨弦衆聽
鮮不詆媒者而難乎才矣玆
何也則以昔之黔士視而不
以今之黔士視也繇斯以談
===
今日爲若謀所以上報
天子下弗愧于中原士卽鞭弭自
倍猶懼退舍何則婉足久而
未易伸也且爾諸士業已鼓
舞其氣效奇于佔俾中稱曰
賢者賢者弗易稱名與實有
當察者若曰吾以是媒祿利
punctuated: 之士釋荷而來也，少自適，上則以繡緣繡，而以素緣素，其懿灼然。黔士之用于世也，少不力，則獨行衆指，獨弦衆聽，鮮不詆媒者，而難乎才矣。玆何也？則以昔之黔士視，而不以今之黔士視也。繇斯以談，今日爲若謀所以上報天子、下弗愧于中原士，卽鞭弭自倍，猶懼退舍。何則？婉足久而未易伸也。且爾諸士業已鼓舞其氣，效奇于佔俾中，稱曰「賢者」。賢者弗易稱，名與實有當察者。若曰「吾以是媒祿利
translation_en: … scholars lay down their rustic burdens and come forward, if they merely conduct themselves with modest ease, those above match brocade with brocade and plain silk with plain silk, and their excellence shines forth clearly. Yet when scholars of Qian [Guizhou] are employed in the world, if they slacken even slightly in their efforts, they walk alone while the crowd points at them, or play a solitary string while the crowd listens; rarely do they escape detraction and slander, making it hard for their talents to prevail. Why is this? It is because people view them as the scholars of Qian of old, rather than as the scholars of Qian of today. Speaking from this perspective, as I take counsel for you today on how you may repay the Son of Heaven above and not feel ashamed before the scholars of the Central Plain below, even if you redouble your efforts with whip and bow, you must still fear falling behind by a stage of march. Why so? Because when one's feet have been cramped and bent for a long time, it is not easy to stretch them out. Moreover, all you scholars have already roused your spirit and displayed extraordinary skill in your textual studies, earning the title of "worthy men." Yet "worthy man" is not an easy title to bear, and the relationship between name and reality is something that must be carefully examined. If you say, "I use this merely as a means to procure emolument and profit…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
已也則氣雖作也一時勸時衰
譬之決塘非不洶湧易竭矣
夫苟實欲爲賢者以俾贊
王治而翼
聖道也則自束髮以至沒齒自牽
絲以至懸紱何所不當砥礪
何所不當鼓舞是猶萬川之
===
赴大溟經晝夜歷四時安有
窮也嗚呼知所以作其氣又
知所以辨其志擷英茹實與
中原士爭伏周孔之軌躅然
後可以爲賢者賢者可以綺
離無根荄之言爲哉
直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣
punctuated:
已也，則氣雖作也一時，勸時衰，譬之決塘，非不洶湧，易竭矣。夫苟實欲爲賢者，以俾贊王治而翼聖道也，則自束髮以至沒齒，自牽絲以至懸紱，何所不當砥礪？何所不當鼓舞？是猶萬川之赴大溟，經晝夜、歷四時，安有窮也？嗚呼！知所以作其氣，又知所以辨其志，擷英茹實，與中原士爭伏周、孔之軌躅，然後可以爲賢者。賢者可以綺麗無根荄之言爲哉？

直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣
translation_en:
…and nothing more, then even if their spirit is roused for a moment, when the encouragement passes it will decline; like breaching a pond, it is not that it fails to surge, but that it is easily exhausted. Yet if they truly desire to become worthy men, so as to assist the Kingly Governance and support the Way of the Sages, then from binding up their hair in youth until the end of their days, and from first entering office until retiring from service, in what should they not temper and refine themselves, and in what should they not rouse and inspire themselves? This is like ten thousand streams rushing toward the great ocean, passing through day and night and traversing the four seasons—how could it ever be exhausted? Alas! Only when they know how to rouse their spirit and also know how to discern their ambition, plucking the blossoms and savoring the fruit, and vying with the scholars of the Central Plains in following the tracks of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, can they be worthy men. How could a worthy man be made by ornate words without root or substance?

[By the]… of Xinghua County in Gaoyou Department, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili)…

title: 萬曆十年貴州鄉試錄
text: 儒學教諭孫繼先謹序
punctuated: 儒學教諭孫繼先謹序。
translation_en: …Instructor of the Confucian School, Sun Jixian 孫繼先, respectfully writes this postface.
